title: Online mistake lower bounds at arbitrary width: two nonlinear variants and a tanh obstruction
status: Conventional proofs with independent AI-agent mathematical checks; not Lean formalized.
review_scope: Independent full review of all seven assembled sources, including exact theorem/proof correspondence, the larger-perturbation corollary with exactly 2^(k-1) forced rounds, its IID extension, posterior mixtures, teacher complexity, and both tanh appendices. All seven source hashes match the final review snapshot. No mathematical correction was required; the IID extension was made locally self-contained by spelling out its constant.

finite_certificate.execution: All exact Fraction assertions passed; independently replayed by the full-manuscript reviewer.

visual_check: The original title/author page, main theorem pages, IID-corollary page, and final certificate page were inspected. After the larger-perturbation addition, rendered pages 7 and 8 containing its complete proof and the revised IID statement/proof were inspected; no clipping or malformed mathematical rendering observed.
critical_scope: Near-identity activation depends on target size and depth; allowed deviation is uniform in learner width.
The larger-perturbation corollary permits a deviation of order 4^(-k)/[(L-1)sqrt(k)] and guarantees exactly 2^(k-1) designated mistakes; the same IID upper bound applies.
Fixed GELU/SiLU/ReLU/leaky-ReLU/softplus result has only one nonlinear hidden layer and no biases.
Every fixed finite width is covered; the positive-scale threshold may depend on width.
IID upper bound is for the same near-identity learner and target; sample count is independent of width and depth, while scale and activation may depend on them.
Tanh comparisons concern scalar or replicated-scalar implementation energies; no conclusion about the wider posterior or all wider implementations of wrong functions.
The all-high-width fixed-standard-activation fully nonlinear biased case remains open.
